L141-D01.text: Last week, my four-year-old daughter, Sally, was invited to a children's party.

L141-D02.text: I decided to take her by train.

L141-D03.text: Sally was very excited because she had never travelled on a train before.

L141-D04.text: She sat near the window and asked questions about everything she saw.

L141-D05.text: Suddenly, a middle-aged lady got on the train and sat opposite Sally.

L141-D07.text: Sally did not answer, but looked at her curiously.

L141-D08.text: The lady was dressed in a blue coat and a large, funny hat.

L141-D09.text: After the train had left the station, the lady opened her handbag and took out her powder compact.

L141-D10.text: She then began to make up her face.

L141-D11.text: 'Why are you doing that?' Sally asked.

L141-D12.text: 'To make myself beautiful,' the lady answered.

L141-D13.text: She put away her compact and smiled kindly.

L141-D14.text: 'But you are still ugly,' Sally said.

L141-D15.text: Sally was amused, but I was very embarrassed!

L143-D01.text: I live in a very old town which is surrounded by beautiful woods.

L143-D02.text: It is a famous beauty spot.

L143-D03.text: On Sundays, hundreds of people come from the city to see our town and to walk through the woods.

L143-D04.text: Visitors have been asked to keep the woods clean and tidy.

L143-D05.text: Litter baskets have been placed under the trees, but people still throw their rubbish everywhere.

L143-D06.text: Last Wednesday, I went for a walk in the woods.

L143-D07.text: What I saw made me very sad.

L143-D08.text: I counted seven old cars and three old refrigerators.

L143-D09.text: The litter baskets were empty and the ground was covered with pieces of paper, cigarette ends, old tyres, empty bottles and rusty tins.

L143-D10.text: Among the rubbish, I found a sign which said, 'Anyone who leaves litter in these woods will be prosecuted!'
